facts.raw_span: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens
areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles

a comprehensive workup—including a TORCH panel, platelet count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, plasminogen levels, von Willebrand factor, factor V Leiden, protein S, protein C, and antiplatelet antibodies—returned within normal limits

concepts.why: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and a roughened-appearing choroid plexus are consistent with congenital CMV infection, which can cause fetal brain abnormalities.

concepts.preferred_label: Fetal Brain Anomalies due to Toxoplasmosis
concepts.why: The ultrasound findings of bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and a roughened-appearing choroid plexus can be seen in toxoplasmosis, which can cause fetal brain anomalies.

concepts.preferred_label: Fetal Ventriculomegaly due to Unknown Etiology
concepts.why: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly with no clear etiology, despite a comprehensive workup, suggests an idiopathic or unknown cause.

The presence of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles, along with hyperechoic regions, can be seen in neonatal hemochromatosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Fetal Infection due to Parvovirus B19
concepts.why: The ultrasound findings of bilateral ventriculomegaly and hyperechoic regions can be seen in parvovirus B19 infection, which can cause fetal anemia and hydrops.

concepts.preferred_label: Fetal Ventriculomegaly due to Congenital Infection
concepts.why: It explains the irregular ventricular walls found in the fetal ultrasound.

rationales.F05: Bilateral ventriculomegaly is a key feature of fetal brain anomalies, including those due to congenital infections and unknown etiologies.
rationales.F06: Irregular ventricular walls are often seen in fetal brain anomalies, particularly those due to congenital infections.
rationales.F07: Hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens may indicate the presence of a congenital infection or other fetal brain anomaly.
rationales.F08: A roughened-appearing choroid plexus can be a sign of fetal brain anomaly, including those due to congenital infections.
rationales.F10: Bilateral ventricular enlargement is a key feature of fetal ventriculomegaly, which can be due to various etiologies, including congenital infections and unknown causes.
rationales.F11: Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles may indicate the presence of a congenital infection or other fetal brain anomaly.
rationales.F12: A comprehensive workup with normal results makes it less likely that the fetal ventriculomegaly is due to a congenital infection or other identifiable cause.
